newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada January wholesale trade rises from December.
newsitem.headline: Canada January wholesale trade rises from December.

text.p: Canada's wholesale trade rose 1.4 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in January from December at C$22.14 billion, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.
Sales, adj C$22.14 bln +1.4 pct +10.5 pct
Inventories, adj C$32.20 bln +0.2 pct +1.4 pct
Note - dollar figures are billions. Other figures are percentage changes.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.4 percent month-on-month rise in January wholesale trade.
StatsCan also revised its figure for December sales to C$21.84 billion from C$21.72 billion.
Statistics Canada said monthly sales increased 10.5 percent over the last year, compared to a 2.8 percent decline in 1995.

Seven of the 11 trade groups, representing 84 percent of all sales for January, showed increases, the agency said. The lumber and building materials industry was particularly dynamic, gaining 23 percent over the year and 1.3 percent on the month, reflecting a stronger housing market.

The federal agency said inventories continued to rise at a moderate pace, up 0.2 percent in January to reach C$32.2 billion. However, since the growth in total sales by wholesalers outpaced the growth in inventories, the inventories to sales ratio fell to 1.45 in January from 1.47 in December.

Wholesalers of computers, packaged software and other electronic products continued to increase inventories in January, rising 1.4 percent from December, Statscan said. Since the middle of 1995, however, sales have kept pace with accumulating stocks, helping the inventory to sales ratio drop to 0.96 in January 1997 from 1.01 in May 1995.
